scoring_justification: The full static molecular simulation (Lennard‑Jones, electrostatic, induction summation over 10×41×41 carbon atoms) is too heavy for the verifier sandbox; comparing the computed q_st^o(H) curve maxima to the paper‑reported values with tolerance is the strongest feasible check.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference maximum q_st^o values and peak H ranges for four polar molecule/orientation combinations.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from the paper: water orientation 1 max q_st^o ≈ 0.35 eV (Fig.6, text); ammonia orientation 2 ≈ 0.27 eV (Fig.7c, text); methanol orientation 2 ≈ 0.44 eV (Fig.8c, text); ethanol orientation 3 ≈ 0.62 eV (Fig.9c, text). Peak positions all between 2.5–4.5 Å. These values match the reference oracle solve.sh which writes curves with those peaks.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values taken from paper text/figures and cross‑checked with the reference solver output that produces these curves exactly.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's actual reported isosteric heat maxima for the specified orientations; they are consistent with the reference solution and serve as the hidden gold.

output_contract.notes: Each CSV must contain at least one row. The hidden checker will extract the maximum q_st^o and the associated H value for scoring.
